verdicts.note: Use another letter for the input position on fourier-transform (for example i), since j is the earlier exponent of the root in the roots-of-unity distinctness argument; the page's disclaimer does not stop a reader from arriving with the exponent meaning.

Use another letter for the output position on fourier-transform (for example q), since k is the power exponent marking which power of omega is meant on roots-of-unity; the disclaimer does not replace renaming.
Use another letter for the digit width on convolution-reduction (for example w), since b is the second input sequence on cyclic-convolution.
Use another letter for the axis count on chinese-remainder-address-map (for example p), since d is the size of the network's matrices on address-interchange.
Use another letter for the input role count on recursive-power-saving (for example R_in or q), since W is the wire count, scratch wires included, on address-interchange.
Use another letter for the smaller-call count on recursive-power-saving (for example c), since s is the field index of H on address-shear.
Use another letter for the parameter growth factor on recursive-power-saving (for example q), since m is the row count of A on lower-triangular-factorization.
Use another letter for the saving exponent on recursive-power-saving (for example e), since gamma is a basis vector of Y on tensor-product.

Use another letter for the saving exponent on recursive-power-saving (for example e), since gamma is the cost ratio R/W on address-interchange; the saving exponent is the logarithm of that ratio, not the ratio itself.
Use another letter for the identity constant on gaussian-resampling (for example K), since C is the per-level work constant on address-interchange.
Use another letter for the first contraction on gaussian-resampling (for example M_1), since L_1 is the prime length of the first axis on chinese-remainder-address-map.
Use another letter for the wrapped coefficient on bluestein-chirp (for example c), since gamma is a basis vector of Y on tensor-product.
Use another letter for the wrapped coefficient on bluestein-chirp (for example c), since gamma is the cost ratio R/W on address-interchange.
